Our Jurisdiction

We investigate the past. Not the future.

Everything we take on has already happened — and what has happened leaves a record: in filings, photographs, messages, memories, and paper. Our work is finding that record and reading it correctly.

Modern Law Enforcement

Watching for what might happen

Today's investigators are geared toward possible crimes — threats assessed, plots interrupted, offenses stopped before they're committed. Necessary work, pointed at the future.

Private Eye

Solving what already happened

We work the other direction. The crime, the fraud, the wrong is already committed — what's missing is the proof. The arts of solving crimes after the fact are old arts, and they are our forte: records, timelines, witnesses, and evidence that still holds up.

The Method

Built like an audit, because it is one

Most investigations start from a blank page. Ours doesn't. Before any fieldwork begins, the file is already built — every fact the records support is in place, and everything else waits, visibly blank, until it's proven. The methods themselves are proven and ironclad — tested over a long history of solved cases, and unchanged where it counts.

1

Confidential intake

You tell us the matter once, in confidence. We tell you honestly whether it's a case we can work — and what it would take.

2

Records first

Case numbers, dates, filings, addresses, histories — everything the public and licensed records actually support is pulled and prefilled into your file.

3

Documented fieldwork

Interviews, observation, and verification — each entry dated, sourced, and filed as it happens. No reconstructed memories weeks later.

4

The report

Findings stated plainly, each one tied to its evidence. What couldn't be established is listed as unknown. A blank is the honest state — we never invent to fill a gap.

HOW A FILE IS BUILTWorked Example
Case numberFilled — from the court record
Hearing datesFilled — from the calendar
Subject historyFilled — from public records
Current whereabouts______________ — fieldwork pending
Motive______________ — not established
ConclusionWritten only when the record carries it

Why it matters: the heavy lifting is done before you ever see the file, so the investigation starts from solid ground — and so do you, your attorney, or anyone who has to act on it.

The Inspector

The white hat is the point

Every office needs a mark. Ours is the Inspector — skull, gears, magnifying glass, and a white hat. The white hat because this work is done on the right side of the line: lawful methods, honest records, nothing planted and nothing exaggerated.

The skull because the truth doesn't care how long it's been buried. The gears because an investigation is a mechanism — every part has to turn, in order, and be able to show its work. The glass because most answers are already there, just too small to read at a glance.

We don't allege. We find.A finding is stated when the record supports it. A suspicion is labeled a suspicion.
All sides, on the record.There's her side, his side, and somewhere in the middle what really happened. We collect all of it.
No threats. Action.Doing nothing and threatening to do something are equally useless. We do the work.
The file outlives the case.Every report is built to still stand up when someone reads it a year from now.

"Somewhere in the middle is what really happened. That's where we dig."

Questions

Before you call

Is my case confidential?

Yes. The consultation, the file, and the report belong to you. Nothing about your matter is discussed with anyone outside the work you've authorized — that's the entire point of hiring an independent investigator instead of asking around.

What will it cost?

It depends on the case, and anyone who quotes a flat price before hearing the matter is guessing with your money. After the intake brief, you get a clear scope and cost before any billable work begins — no open-ended meters, no surprises.

What do I actually receive?

A written report: what was checked, what was found, the evidence for each finding, and — stated just as plainly — what could not be established. Dated, sourced, and built to be handed to an attorney, an employer, or an agency.

Can you guarantee you'll find what I'm looking for?

No honest investigator guarantees a result. People move, records are sealed, memories fail. What we guarantee is the method: every applicable record checked, every lead worked, and a report that shows its work either way.

Do you work with attorneys?

Yes — legal support is one of our core services. We can work directly with your attorney, and if a matter turns out to need one, the file we build is the file they'll want to start from.

Is everything you do legal?

Yes, and it has to be — evidence gathered unlawfully is worthless to you and a liability to everyone. We work from public records, licensed databases, interviews, and lawful observation. The white hat isn't a costume; it's the method.
